newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bourse to open later Weds after accord.
newsitem.headline: Greek bourse to open later Weds after accord.

text.p: The Athens bourse will resume trading later today but only firms that have settled accounts with the clearing house will be allowed to trade, Panayiotis Kondalexis, the president of the 65-member Associaton of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA), told Reuters.

"We reached an agreement with the national economy minister last night and the bourse will open today but only those firms that have settled with the clearing house will be allowed to trade," said Kondalexis.
He added that opening would be delayed but he did not specify the time. Trading regularly starts at 1045 local.
"All firms should be trading by Thursday," said Kondalexis.
SMEHA asked for a fast clearing of all accounts on Wednesday and for a 15-30 minute delay in opening to facilitate the process in its meeting with National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou.
The delay could be made up after the regular closing time, Kondalexis told reporters on Wednesday.

The Athens stock exchange has stayed closed for the last three business days on a settlement row after it was discovered that brokerage Delta Securities allegedly tried to pay 2.6 billion drachma ($10.9 million) settlement fees to the exchange's clearing house with bad cheques.

Three officials at Delta Securities have already been charged with fraud by a Greek prosecutor and the offices of the firm have been sealed. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 ($ = 238.2 Greek Drachmas)
